title: Issue management approach, issue register and issue report
blurb: State the purpose of the issue management approach, issue register and issue report, and choose the right one in an agile project.
question: A request for change would add a new Must have to the agreed project backlog. Which product describes its impacts and recommends a decision, and which one records it so its status can be tracked?

teach.h: Three issue products, kept in agile
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile keeps the three issues-practice management products, tailored for agile. The issue management approach describes how issues will be captured and reported and how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled. The issue register records the formal issues being managed. The issue report describes one issue's impacts on the baseline, the options for resolving it and a recommended decision.

head: Product
Purpose
Think of it as
rows: How issues are captured, reported and controlled
Record of formal issues and their status
One issue's impacts, options and recommendation
teach.caption: Book references: Table 11.1, 11.3.4, Table 12.1.

teach.h: The agile twist: change is embraced
teach.body: In an agile project, the issue management approach recognises that iterative and incremental working creates many product versions and inevitable change, which should be embraced and supported. So the approach sets out a light route for detail changes handled at team level and a formal route for changes that affect the baseline. It is one of the management approaches agreed in initiating a project, often co-created in the project initiation workshop.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 11.1, Table 13.6, Table 13.7

teach.body: Not every issue goes in the issue register. Informal issues, along with required actions and significant events, are noted in the daily log, which the project manager creates in starting up a project. Formal issues, such as requests for change that affect the baseline, are recorded in the issue register so their status can be tracked until they are closed. Project support often helps by maintaining these records.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book Table 12.1, Table 13.1

rows.label: Trigger
values: A formal issue needs a decision

rows.label: Content
values: Options and recommendation for the plan

teach.body: Project manager Bethan Hughes is running an agile project for a tenant repairs portal. A request arrives to add a new landlord module as a Must have, which would add an epic to the agreed project backlog. Project support officer Kieran Walsh logs it in the issue register. Bethan writes an issue report setting out the effect on the project backlog and release map, two options and her recommendation, and the board decides. A minor wording tweak raised the same day is noted in her daily log and handled by the team.

teach.text: The issue management approach is the procedure, not a list of issues: the issues themselves go in the issue register. And an issue report is for one issue's impacts and options; when a stage or project is forecast to exceed tolerance, the product is an exception report.

items: Issue management approach: how issues are captured and reported, and how baseline changes are assessed and controlled (Table 11.1).
Agile tailoring: inevitable change is embraced and supported.
Issue register: record of formal issues and their status.
Issue report: an issue's impacts on the baseline, options and a recommended decision.
Daily log: informal issues, actions and events. Exception report: forecast tolerance breach.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the issue management approach, issue register and issue report in an agile project. You can also choose between the issue register and the daily log, and between an issue report and an exception report.

A.q: What does the issue management approach describe?
options: The status and owner of each open formal issue
One issue's impacts, options and recommended decision
The total risk exposure tracked across the iterations
How issues are captured and baseline changes controlled
A.why: The issue management approach describes how issues will be captured and reported and how changes to the project baseline will be assessed and controlled (Table 11.1).

whyNot.0: Status and owner of each formal issue are held in the issue register.
whyNot.1: One issue's impacts, options and recommendation are in an issue report.
whyNot.2: Total risk exposure is shown by the cumulative risk burn-down chart.

A.q: What is the purpose of an issue report?
options: To forecast a breach of the agreed stage tolerance
To list every formal issue raised on the project
To describe how issues will be managed on the project
To set out an issue's impacts and a recommendation
A.why: An issue report describes the issue's impacts on the project baseline, identifies ways to resolve it and recommends a decision (Table 11.1).

whyNot.0: A forecast breach of tolerance is reported in an exception report.
whyNot.1: The issue register records the formal issues.
whyNot.2: How issues will be managed is described in the issue management approach.

A.q: What does the issue register hold?
options: A record of the formal issues being managed
The procedure for controlling baseline changes
The project manager's informal notes and actions
The options and recommendation for one issue
A.why: The issue register captures and maintains the formal issues being managed, with their status (11.3.4).

whyNot.1: The procedure belongs in the issue management approach.
whyNot.2: Informal notes and actions go in the daily log.
whyNot.3: Options and a recommendation for one issue are in an issue report.

B.q: A project manager notes a minor informal issue and a follow-up action that need no formal handling. Where should these be recorded?
options: Issue register
Issue report
Daily log
Lessons log
B.why: The daily log records informal issues, required actions and significant events (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The issue register is for formal issues.
whyNot.1: An issue report is prepared for a formal issue needing a decision.
whyNot.3: The lessons log records lessons, not informal issues and actions.

B.q:
Which two statements about issue products in PRINCE2 Agile are correct?
1. The issue management approach treats inevitable change as something to embrace.
2. The issue register describes how baseline changes will be controlled.
3. An issue report recommends a decision on the issue.
4. An exception report is raised for every request for change.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: The approach embraces inevitable change in agile (1), and the issue report recommends a decision (3) (Table 11.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: controlling baseline changes is described in the approach, not the register.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: the register records issues, and exception reports are for forecast tolerance breaches.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: an exception report is for a forecast tolerance breach, not each request.

B.q: A formal request for change needs a board decision, and no tolerance is forecast to be exceeded. Which report should the project manager prepare?
options: Issue report
Exception report
Highlight report
End stage report
B.why: An issue report sets out the issue's impacts, options and a recommended decision; no exception report is needed while tolerances hold (Table 11.1).

whyNot.1: An exception report is for a forecast breach of stage or project tolerance.
whyNot.2: A highlight report, or project dashboard, gives regular status, not a decision on one issue.
whyNot.3: An end stage report supports the stage boundary decision, not a single issue.

C.q: Which workshop topic co-creates the management approaches, including the issue management approach, and in which process?
options: Risk analysis topic; starting up a project
Project highlights topic; controlling a stage
Management approaches topic; initiating a project
Agilometer assessment review; directing a project
C.why: The project initiation workshop has a management approaches topic to co-create them; agreeing the management approaches is an activity of initiating a project (Tables 13.6, 13.7).

whyNot.0: Risk analysis is a topic of the starting up and project canvas workshops, not where approaches are co-created.
whyNot.1: Project highlights is a progress review topic for reviewing dashboard metrics.
whyNot.3: The Agilometer review is an agile enablement workshop topic about agile-adoption risk.

C.q: A problem means the remaining Must haves for the stage can no longer be delivered. Which report is needed, and why?
options: Issue report, because the problem affects a product being built
Exception report, because tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
Highlight report, because the board needs regular status
Lessons report, because the problem should not recur
C.why: Failing to deliver the Must haves forecasts a breach of tolerance, which needs an exception report with options and a recommendation (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: An issue report covers an issue within tolerance; a forecast breach needs an exception report.
whyNot.2: Regular status does not deal with a forecast breach of tolerance.
whyNot.3: Lessons are captured, but the immediate need is an exception report to the board.

C.q: A request for change that affects the baseline has been raised. Where is it recorded so its status can be tracked until it is closed, and who commonly helps maintain that record?
options: Daily log; the team coach
Risk register; project assurance
Product backlog; the product owner
Issue register; project support
C.why: Formal issues are recorded and tracked in the issue register, and project support commonly helps with risk and change management records (11.3.4, Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: The daily log is the PM's informal record, and the team coach does not maintain it.
whyNot.1: A request for change is an issue, not a risk, and assurance monitors rather than administers.
whyNot.2: A baseline change is not just added to a product backlog; it is recorded and decided formally.

reteach.title: The rulebook, the logbook and the briefing note
reteach.question: How can three office documents help you keep the issue products apart?

blocks.body: The office rulebook says how complaints are handled: that is the issue management approach. The complaints logbook lists every formal complaint and its status: that is the issue register. The briefing note to the director on one complaint, with options and a recommendation, is the issue report. A sticky note on your own desk for small things is the daily log.

blocks.text: How = approach. Which formal issues = register. One issue's case for a decision = report. Forecast tolerance breach = exception report.

explain.body: Describes how issues will be captured and reported and how changes to the baseline will be assessed and controlled. In agile, inevitable change is embraced and supported.

test.q: How should the issue management approach be tailored for an agile project?
options: By requiring board approval for each story change
By embracing the inevitable change agile produces
By replacing it with the risk management approach
By holding change requests until the final stage
test.why: In agile, multiple product versions make change inevitable, and the approach says it should be embraced and supported (Table 11.1).

whyNot.0: Detail changes are handled at team level; the board decides baseline changes.
whyNot.2: Risk and issues keep separate approaches; one does not replace the other.
whyNot.3: Holding back change contradicts agile's embrace of it.

explain.body: The record of formal issues being managed, with their status, kept until each issue is closed. Informal issues go in the daily log instead.

test.q: Where are formal issues recorded and tracked?
options: In the daily log
In the lessons log
In the issue register
In the risk register
test.why: Formal issues are recorded and tracked in the issue register (11.3.4).

whyNot.0: The daily log holds informal issues, actions and events.
whyNot.1: The lessons log holds lessons to learn from.
whyNot.3: The risk register holds risks, which are uncertain, not issues.

explain.body: Describes one issue's impacts on the project baseline, identifies ways to resolve it or to address an off-specification, and recommends a decision.

test.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. An [?] describes an issue's impacts on the project baseline and recommends a decision.
options: issue register
issue report
exception report
highlight report
test.why: The issue report describes the issue's impacts on the baseline, identifies ways to resolve it and recommends a decision (Table 11.1).

whyNot.0: The issue register records formal issues; it does not analyse one.
whyNot.2: An exception report covers a forecast breach of tolerance.
whyNot.3: A highlight report gives regular stage status.

explain.body: An issue within tolerance that needs a decision gets an issue report. If a stage or project is forecast to exceed tolerance, the PM raises an exception report.

test.q: When is an exception report needed instead of an issue report?
options: When a stage is forecast to exceed tolerance
When a request for change comes from users
When an issue is informal and minor
When the team has swarmed on a blocker
test.why: An exception report is used when a stage or project plan is forecast to exceed tolerance (Table 12.1).

whyNot.1: A request for change within tolerance is handled with an issue report.
whyNot.2: Informal minor issues go in the daily log.
whyNot.3: Swarming is a team technique; it does not trigger an exception report.
